name: Delivery challan — transportation of goods without an invoice
definition: A delivery challan is issued under rule 55(1) in lieu of an invoice at the time of removal of goods, in four cases: liquid gas of unknown quantity, goods sent for job work, movement for reasons other than supply, and other supplies notified by the Board. Rule 55(1) fixes nine particulars, (i) to (ix).
why_it_exists: Goods move for reasons that are not sales. A delivery challan documents the movement without asserting a supply, which is precisely why it must never be posted as one.
inputs: whether the movement is for supply to the consignee
outputs: the set of rule 55(1) particulars found
the set of mandatory particulars absent
whether an invoice is still owed
preconditions: goods are being removed for transportation
the case falls within rule 55(1)(a) to (d)
exceptions: clause (vii), tax rate and tax amount, applies only where the transportation is for supply to the consignee
clause (v) permits a provisional quantity where the exact quantity is not known
rule 55(5) governs semi knocked down and completely knocked down consignments, where one invoice covers several challans
common_mistakes: posting a delivery challan as a purchase or a sale — three of its four cases are not supplies at all
treating a job-work challan as a sale to the job worker
counting each challan in a knocked-down shipment as a separate supply, when rule 55(5) puts one complete invoice before the first consignment
expecting the rule 46(q) signature formula — clause (ix) says only 'signature.'
gst_references: UNKNOWN — which further supplies the Board has notified under rule 55(1)(d) is fixed by notification and no notification is held locally
UNKNOWN — source is the Rules as at 01-01-2022; later amendments not held locally
evidence_required: the stated reason for the movement
the later tax invoice, where the movement was for supply
confidence_factors: weak when the document does not state why the goods are moving, because that is what decides whether a supply happened
weak when a challan issued for a supply has no matching later invoice
validation_checks: all nine particulars (i) to (ix) are present, subject to (vii) and (viii) applying conditionally
no revenue or purchase is posted from a delivery challan alone
where the movement was for supply to the recipient, a later tax invoice exists
the challan is declared as specified in rule 138 where it travels in lieu of an invoice
examples: a challan for goods sent to a job worker, showing consigner and consignee GSTINs, HSN, description, quantity, taxable value and signature, with no tax amount
counterexamples: a challan posted to the sales ledger — rule 55(1)(c) movements are expressly for reasons other than by way of supply

evidence.quote: the consigner may issue a delivery challan, serially numbered not exceeding sixteen characters, in one or multiple series, in lieu of invoice at the time of removal of goods for transportation, containing the following details, namely:-
transportation of goods for reasons other than by way of supply, or
Where goods are being transported on a delivery challan in lieu of invoice, the same shall be declared as specified in rule 138.

Where the goods being transported are for the purpose of supply to the recipient but the tax invoice could not be issued at the time of removal of goods for the purpose of supply, the supplier shall issue a tax invoice after delivery of goods.
